title: Memory Leaks in Java
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of memory leaks in java and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—unintended object retention—in a small, readable example.
Identify one failure, compatibility, security, or resource-management concern and describe a safe response.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study memory leaks in java with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you base runtime tuning on repeatable measurements and diagnostic evidence. In this lesson, focus on unintended object retention and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

items.text: JVM performance work begins with evidence. common_mistakes.problem: Assuming one timing or memory observation proves a performance conclusion.
common_mistakes.why: JIT warm-up, scheduling, allocation, and workload changes can distort single measurements.
common_mistakes.fix: Use repeatable workloads and appropriate JDK diagnostics, and record the environment.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.
